slides.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
slides.content:
# Deep Learning 🧠

Powerful neural networks that learn hierarchical representations!

## What you'll learn:
- **Neural Networks and Activation Functions** - Building blocks
- **CNNs and RNNs** - For images and sequences
- **Training Methods** - Making models learn

## Deep Learning vs Machine Learning

```
Traditional ML:
Raw Data → Hand-crafted Features → Model → Output

Deep Learning:
Raw Data → Neural Network (learns features!) → Output
```

## Why Deep Learning?

- 🖼️ **Image recognition** - Better than humans!
- 🗣️ **Speech recognition** - Siri, Alexa
- 📝 **Natural language** - ChatGPT, translation
- 🎮 **Game AI** - AlphaGo, game bots

> 💡 **Deep learning excels when you have lots of data!**

slides.title: Neural Networks Basics
slides.content:
# Neural Network Architecture 🏗️

## Structure

```
Input Layer → Hidden Layer(s) → Output Layer
   [X]    →     [Neurons]    →    [y]
```

## Basic Neural Network

```python
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras

model = keras.Sequential([
    # Input layer (784 features)
    keras.layers.Input(shape=(784,)),
    
    # Hidden layers
    keras.layers.Dense(128, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    
    # Output layer (10 classes)
    keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])
```

## Neuron Computation

```
Neuron:
1. Weighted sum: z = w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + b
2. Activation: a = activation(z)
```

## PyTorch Alternative

```python
import torch.nn as nn

class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(784, 128)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, 64)
        self.fc3 = nn.Linear(64, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = torch.relu(self.fc2(x))
        x = self.fc3(x)
        return x
```

slides.title: Activation Functions
slides.content:
# Activation Functions ⚡

Add non-linearity to neural networks!

## Common Activations

### ReLU (Most Popular)
```python
# f(x) = max(0, x)
keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu')

# Pros: Fast, avoids vanishing gradient
# Cons: Can "die" (output 0 for all inputs)
```

### Sigmoid
```python
# f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x))  → Output: 0 to 1
keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')  # Binary classification
```

### Softmax (Multi-class)
```python
# Converts to probabilities that sum to 1
keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')  # 10 classes
```

### Tanh
```python
# f(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / (e^x + e^(-x))  → Output: -1 to 1
keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='tanh')
```

## When to Use Which?

| Activation | Use Case |
|------------|----------|
| ReLU | Hidden layers (default) |
| Sigmoid | Binary output (0/1) |
| Softmax | Multi-class probabilities |
| Tanh | When you need negative values |

> 💡 **Use ReLU for hidden layers, Sigmoid/Softmax for output!**

slides.title: CNNs for Images
slides.content:
# Convolutional Neural Networks 📷

Specialized for image processing!

## Key Components

```
Convolution → Pooling → Convolution → Pooling → Dense → Output
```

## CNN Architecture

```python
model = keras.Sequential([
    # Convolutional layers
    keras.layers.Conv2D(32, (3, 3), activation='relu', input_shape=(28, 28, 1)),
    keras.layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
    
    keras.layers.Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
    
    keras.layers.Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation='relu'),
    
    # Dense layers
    keras.layers.Flatten(),
    keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])
```

## What Each Layer Does

| Layer | Purpose |
|-------|--------|
| Conv2D | Detect features (edges, shapes) |
| MaxPooling2D | Reduce size, keep important info |
| Flatten | Convert 2D to 1D for Dense |
| Dense | Classification |

## CNN Applications

- 🖼️ Image classification
- 👤 Face recognition
- 🚗 Self-driving cars
- 🏥 Medical imaging

> 💡 **CNNs learn features automatically** - no manual feature engineering!

slides.title: RNNs for Sequences
slides.content:
# Recurrent Neural Networks 📝

Process sequential data with memory!

## Why RNNs?

```
Sentence: "I love Python programming"

Regular NN: Looks at each word independently
RNN: Remembers context from previous words
```

## LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory)

```python
model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Embedding(vocab_size, 128),
    keras.layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences=True),
    keras.layers.LSTM(32),
    keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])
```

## GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit)

```python
model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Embedding(vocab_size, 128),
    keras.layers.GRU(64),
    keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])
```

## RNN Applications

| Application | Example |
|-------------|--------|
| Text classification | Sentiment analysis |
| Language modeling | Text generation |
| Machine translation | English → French |
| Speech recognition | Audio → Text |
| Time series | Stock prediction |

## LSTM vs GRU

```
LSTM: More parameters, handles long sequences better
GRU: Simpler, trains faster, often similar performance
```

> 💡 **Use LSTM/GRU instead of basic RNN** to avoid vanishing gradients!

slides.title: Training Methods
slides.content:
# Training Neural Networks 🎓

## Compile and Train

```python
model.compile(
    optimizer='adam',           # How to update weights
    loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',  # What to minimize
    metrics=['accuracy']        # What to track
)

history = model.fit(
    X_train, y_train,
    epochs=10,                  # Times through data
    batch_size=32,              # Samples per update
    validation_split=0.2        # Hold out for validation
)
```

## Common Optimizers

| Optimizer | Best For |
|-----------|----------|
| Adam | General purpose (default) |
| SGD | Fine-grained control |
| RMSprop | RNNs |

## Preventing Overfitting

```python
# Dropout - Randomly disable neurons
keras.layers.Dropout(0.5)  # 50% dropout

# Early Stopping
early_stop = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
    monitor='val_loss',
    patience=3,
    restore_best_weights=True
)
model.fit(..., callbacks=[early_stop])

# Regularization
keras.layers.Dense(64, kernel_regularizer='l2')
```

## Batch Normalization

```python
keras.layers.BatchNormalization()
# Stabilizes training, enables higher learning rates
```

> 🎯 **Adam optimizer + Dropout + Early Stopping = Good baseline!**

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've learned Deep Learning basics!

## Neural Networks and Activations
- ✅ Layers: Input → Hidden → Output
- ✅ ReLU for hidden, Sigmoid/Softmax for output
- ✅ TensorFlow/Keras or PyTorch

## CNNs for Images
- ✅ Conv2D → Pooling → Dense
- ✅ Learn features automatically
- ✅ Great for image tasks

## RNNs for Sequences
- ✅ LSTM/GRU for text and time series
- ✅ Remember context
- ✅ Handle variable-length sequences

## Training Methods
- ✅ Adam optimizer (default)
- ✅ Dropout for regularization
- ✅ Early stopping
- ✅ Batch normalization

## Quick Model Template

```python
model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Dense(128, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dropout(0.3),
    keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy')
model.fit(X_train, y_train, epochs=10, validation_split=0.2)
```

> 🚀 **Next Steps:** Learn about Model Evaluation!
